answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can release earnings through a slow escrow: each identity's kernel of reputation earns only as verified work accrues, and payouts unlock gradually rather than at once. A public beacon publishes random audit rounds, so a tide of fake identities cannot cash out before sampling catches duplicates. Sybils face delayed rewards and a rising chance of forfeiting escrowed income, while genuine agents keep steady, auditable earnings.
